title: Resiliency presets and idempotency ledgers for SDK streams and unary calls
creator: Lydia Chen
description: Goal: Define pragmatic cross-language defaults and implementation guidance for retries, backoff, and idempotency behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, with explicit streaming ergonomics and a retryable-error taxonomy developers can rely on. Deliverables: 1) three named retry profiles (conservative/balanced/aggressive) for unary ops, 2) a streaming reconnect/resume contract and default behavior, 3) idempotency ledger semantics and TTL guidance, 4) retryable error taxonomy that maps HTTP/network/runtime signals to SDK policies, 5) canonical sample snippets and migration plan for existing clients.
description_short: Cross-SDK defaults for retries/backoff, idempotency semantics, and streaming resume behavior with examples and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose config for retry_profile with values: conservative, balanced, aggressive
Default retry_profile is 'balanced' for newly created clients unless overridden
Streaming auto-reconnect attempts limited and resume attempted when server provides resume_token
Server-side idempotency ledger semantics documented (TTL, dedupe guarantees) and SDKs include helper for idempotency_key generation
Unit + integration tests for retryable-error mapping across Python/TS/Go
Dashboards updated: retried_requests, retry_success_rate, idempotency_hits, streaming_resume_success_rate
technical_notes: Retry profiles (unary): conservative -> max_attempts=3, base_delay=200ms, multiplier=1.8, cap=8s; balanced -> max_attempts=6, base_delay=100ms, multiplier=1.6, cap=10s; aggressive -> max_attempts=10, base_delay=50ms, multiplier=1.5, cap=20s
Use exponential backoff with full jitter (per AWS jitter paper) for all profiles. Implement stable random seed per process for deterministic testability where needed.

Streaming behavior: on transport disconnect, attempt up to 3 resume attempts (default) using resume_token provided by service; if resume_token missing, do not silently replay non-idempotent streams — surface error to caller and provide helper to restart with optional dedupe ID.

Idempotency ledger: server guarantees at-least-once execution deduplication for keys with TTL=72h by default. SDKs should generate v4 UUIDs for idempotency_key by default and expose an option to override per-request.

Idempotency semantics for streaming: recommend using "resume_token" as the canonical stream resumption handle. Do not reuse unary idempotency ledger for live chunked streams; ledger is for final-result dedupe only.

Retryable error taxonomy (high level): network_connectivity (DNS, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT), transport_reset (RST), transient_5xx (500,502,503,504), rate_limit_retryable (HTTP 429 with Retry-After or X-Retry-After), model_resource_temp (503/429 with body code 'MODEL_BUSY' or 'OOM'), idempotency_conflict (409 non-retryable by default), auth_errors (401/403 non-retryable), client_bad_request (400,422 non-retryable), partial_response_stream_cut (stream-specific; retry via resume_token when available).

Mapping guidance: treat 429 with explicit Retry-After as retryable with backoff; 429 without Retry-After rely on profile cap. 5xx almost always retryable except deterministic validation 501/505 which should be surfaced.
Configuration: allow clients to set env var REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_PROFILE or pass retryProfile when constructing client. Provide per-request overrides via request.retry_hint.
Server/contract notes: backend must include optional resume_token in streaming frames and expose idempotency lease/TTL via capability endpoint for clients to display to users.
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize taxonomy and retry_profile knobs; land tests that assert behavior for synthetic failure modes
Week 2: implement SDK helpers (Python/TS/Go), add env var support and builder patterns; small API ergonomic surface to set per-request idempotency_key
Week 3: add streaming resume helper, integration tests against staging runtime, update docs and examples
Week 4: rollout: opt-in canary (20%) -> monitor metrics -> full default flip after 1 week of stable metrics
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: overly-aggressive retries increase duplicate work and cost. Mitigation: conservative default for customer accounts with spend>threshold and per-account override via control plane.
Risk: resume semantics misused leading to inconsistent application state. Mitigation: require explicit resume_token handshake and add clear docs and error types in SDK to avoid silent replays.
Risk: idempotency ledger storage growth. Mitigation: recommend TTL 72h and sampling for extremely high-volume customers; use sharded ledger with LRU eviction for on-prem/private deployments.
migration_notes: Existing clients will keep current behavior until flip. To opt into new behavior prior to default flip, set REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_PROFILE=balanced (or pass retryProfile='balanced' to client constructor). Encourage customers that perform non-idempotent writes to supply idempotency_key to avoid duplicates. Provide a migration tool script that scans codebases for places creating retries manually and suggests SDK-native configs.
test_plan: Unit tests for backoff math and jitter (deterministic seed) in each SDK
Integration harness that injects: TCP resets, synthetic 502/503, 429 with and without Retry-After, and simulated model 'MODEL_BUSY' responses
End-to-end against staging runtime verifying idempotency hits and no duplicates with ledger enabled
Streaming tests: simulate mid-stream disconnect at token offsets and assert resume success when resume_token present
metrics_and_dashboards: dashboard: SDK Retry Health (per-lang panels), Streaming Resume Heatmap, Idempotency Ledger Size by tenant
rollout_plan: Canary: opt-in SDK release (tagged) + config flag for 20% of traffic in runtime routing. Monitor: retry_success_rate >= 95% and duplicate_response_rate < 0.1% for one week before global default flip.
docs_and_examples: SDK samples: python snippet, ts snippet, go snippet included in repo examples/ retry_and_idempotency.md
